opening: We use the dromara/carbon library (current main branch) to format dates, store them in a database, compare them, convert them to the Chinese lunar calendar and take the start and end of a minute, and found six problems.

requirements.m01: Formatting a date with a layout string that ends in a single backslash (the escape character) crashes with an index out of range. A trailing lone backslash must simply be dropped: the layout "Y-m-d\" gives "2020-08-05", a layout that is only a backslash gives an empty string, and an escaped backslash at the end (two backslashes) still prints one backslash.
requirements.m02: When we reuse one date value as the destination for several database rows, scanning a SQL NULL into it reports success but keeps the date from the previous row. This happens for a plain Carbon value and for the DateTime, Timestamp and custom-format field types. After a NULL is scanned, the value must give NULL back to the database, and scanning a real date into it afterwards must still work.
requirements.m03: When the week is configured to start on a day other than Monday, the weekday names come out wrong: 2024-03-10 is a Sunday, but with the week starting on Sunday the full weekday name says Monday, with the week starting on Saturday it says Tuesday, and the short name in formatted output (the D layout letter) says Mon. The weekday name, full and short, in every output method and in the D layout letter, must name the actual day and never depend on the configured week start.
requirements.m04: Taking the start and end of the minute for a time inside the repeated hour when clocks go back can land on the other occurrence of that hour, so the minute does not contain the time: for 2026-11-01 01:34:49.123456789 -05:00 in America/New_York (the second 1 a.m.) the minute comes out as 01:34:00 to 01:34:59.999999999 at -04:00, an hour too early, and for 2026-04-05 01:45:49.123456789 +11:00 in Australia/Lord_Howe, which goes back half an hour, it comes out at 01:45:00 +10:30, half an hour after the time itself. Both boundaries must stay in the time's own occurrence, with its UTC offset, so that the minute contains the time. Zones whose offset includes seconds must keep working as today: in Africa/Monrovia on 1960-06-15 (UTC-00:44:30) the minute of 11:50:19 local time still starts at 11:50:00 local time. As today, the time itself must not change, and the boundaries keep its zone and week start.
requirements.m05: Checking whether two dates fall in the same decade ignores the century: 1995-08-05 and 2095-08-05 are reported as the same decade, and so are 2020-08-05 and 1920-08-05. Only dates of the same decade of the same century may match; 2020-08-05 and 2029-12-31 still do.
requirements.m06: Converting a time to the Chinese lunar calendar gives the previous lunar day for some times just after midnight. We see it in Europe/Berlin, Asia/Kolkata and America/New_York: 2021-06-14 00:00 in Berlin is the Dragon Boat Festival, lunar 2021-05-05, but comes out as 2021-05-04; 2020-06-21 00:15 in Kolkata should be lunar 2020-05-01 and 2020-06-25 00:30 in New York should be 2020-05-05. The same dates at noon already convert correctly. The lunar date must follow the calendar date of the time in its own zone, whatever the time of day.
